question: Why does a film need Foley even for scenes whose production sound was perfect?
answer: For the foreign versions. Dubbing replaces the dialogue track, and every footstep, rustle and clinking cup caught by the same microphone goes out with it. Distributors therefore demand a music-and-effects track with no voices at all, and Foley rebuilds those small noises so an Italian or Japanese dub still sounds inhabited.
move: When one part must be swapped out, check what else it carries.
ask: When I swap out one part of a system, what else was it quietly carrying?
source: Holman, Sound for Film and Television
